fields.category: usage | injury | depth-chart | coaching | trade | other
fields.summary: one factual sentence (fantasy framing), grounded in the source
fields.short_label: optional, DISPLAY ONLY: the front-page headline form of the event, plain words, under 80 chars, what happened with no analysis, no snap counts, no quotes. The summary remains the evidence record. Never read by evidence or verification logic; adding or editing it touches nothing a human verified.
fields.verified: true means a human opened that source_url and confirmed both the event and its date. Nothing else sets this flag - not an agent's confidence, not the URL resolving. All 27 were human-verified on 2026-08-12. Only a verified entry dated inside the move window flips a signal to 'catalyst-confirmed'.
fields.sample: false = real event (all 27). true would render 'SAMPLE - not real'.
fields.bench_reason: present only on bench[] items: why the entry is held out of live entries. Two grounds only - dated outside the snapshot window, or the summary makes a price claim the first-party ADP contradicts.
fields.sources: array of independent reports of the SAME event. Each carries url, outlet, date_text (the publication date exactly as it appears on the fetched page), and kind (original or syndicated). Independence means a distinct newsroom doing its own write-up. Five sites republishing one RotoWire or AP blurb is ONE source, not five. An aggregator that credits another outlet points at that outlet and is not counted separately.
fields.independent_source_count: how many entries in sources[] are independent originators. This is a proxy for REACH, which is the actual mechanism by which news moves ADP: a composite moves only when the news reaches the drafters behind it. One beat writer's practice note does not reach them; a story carried across five newsrooms does. Published like every other threshold in this product.
fields.date_confirmed_on_source: true means at least one source in sources[] DISPLAYS a publication date that was read off the page. false means no source displays a date. unknown means the entry predates this rule and has not been audited. Added because real-002-diggs carried verified:true with a date six days wrong: its source_url renders 'Published:' and 'Updated:' with empty date fields, so the date it claimed was never confirmable from the source it cited. A dateless source cannot verify a date.

_schema.provenance: Entries dated inside the rolling window of the stored 08-10 to 08-12 snapshots. Entries outside it are held in bench[] with source_url intact rather than deleted. NOT ADDED: Darren Waller (CAR) and Deshaun Watson (CLE) are real and in-window but sat outside the tracked pool at the time, so their player pages render 'not tracked', the same reason J.J. McCarthy was never added. Note Mike Evans is on SF in 2026, not TB. On 2026-08-14 the window was widened per the rolling-mean reasoning above, twelve eval-set events were sourced with corroboration counts, and real-002-diggs was corrected from 08-11 to 08-05 and its verification withdrawn. On 2026-08-20 Navi opened the sources for real-043, real-044, real-045, real-047, real-048 and real-049 and confirmed the events and dates; the flags were set at his direction. real-112-dart was removed the same day as an event with no price move attached (the base-rate failure the August lookback test documents). real-046-young is held unverified deliberately: the event is real but its connection to the move is a judgment not yet made.
_schema.rules: Candidates may be sourced by research agents or by hand (ADR-004, amending ADR-002). Every entry carries a primary source_url, no entry without one. Every entry added after 2026-08-14 also carries sources[] with an on-page date read off each page. No scraper, no news API, no NLP pipeline. What an agent may NOT do is set verified:true.
_schema.window: 2026-08-04 .. 2026-08-12. Derived, not hand-picked. the ADP stored at the time was a trailing ~7 day mean, so the 08-10 snapshot averages drafts from 08-04 to 08-10 and the 08-12 snapshot averages 08-06 to 08-12. The move between them is driven only by drafts ENTERING the newer mean (08-11 to 08-12) and drafts LEAVING the older one (08-04 to 08-05); the 08-06 to 08-10 overlap sits in both means and largely cancels. The lookback is therefore the OLDER mean's own start, computed in lib/evidence.ts catalystLookbackStart(). The previous rule, 'on or after the previous snapshot', discarded the entire leaving edge, which is the half whose sign is inverted: a catalyst on the leaving edge pushes the measured move AGAINST its own direction as the reaction ages out.
_schema.corroboration: Reported at 1 to 2 independent sources. Corroborated at 3 or more. The tier is recorded, not yet enforced: no entry is excluded for a low count. The count is suppressed by the window boundary, so the two rules interact and cannot be set independently. Jauan Jennings is the worked example: his 08-12 depth chart event carries 1 in-window source because CBS Minnesota, Vikings Wire and The Viking Age all covered it on 08-13, one day outside. Extend the window a single day and the same event reads 4.
